original_question: Does the Continuum Hypothesis imply realizations of the consistent settings (d), (e), (g), (j), and (l) in the Borel Scheepers-diagram classification presented in Figure 4?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4.1: "Does CH imply a realization of the settings (d),(e),(g),(j), and (l)?" in the Borel-case Scheepers-diagram discussion. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right hypothesis (CH), the right framework (the Borel Scheepers diagram), and exactly the five settings singled out by the paper as the remaining CH cases in Problem 4.1. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))
missing_details: It does not state explicitly that the objects sought are sets of real numbers X ⊆ R. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

It leaves "realization" implicit; in Section 4 this means: for a given set of reals X, place a bullet at each node of the Borel diagram where X satisfies the property and a circle otherwise, and ask for X whose bullet/circle pattern is exactly the designated setting from Figure 4. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

It does not define the Borel cover classes B, BΩ, and BΓ as the families of countable Borel covers, countable Borel ω-covers, and countable Borel γ-covers of X, respectively. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

It does not define the cover notions used in those classes: covers are taken to be nontrivial; an ω-cover covers every finite subset of X; a γ-cover is infinite and contains each x ∈ X in all but finitely many members. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

It does not define the selection principles S1(A,B) and Sfin(A,B), which are part of the meaning of every node in the diagram. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

It does not unpack the five labels (d), (e), (g), (j), and (l) into exact satisfaction-patterns among the seven Borel-case properties in Figure 2, so it is not stand-alone without the figure. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

It does not make explicit that the quantifier is separate for each listed setting: the question is whether CH yields, for each of those five patterns, some set of reals realizing that pattern, not one set realizing all five at once. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))
refined_question: Assume the Continuum Hypothesis. For a set of reals X ⊆ R, let B, BΩ, and BΓ denote the families of countable Borel covers, countable Borel ω-covers, and countable Borel γ-covers of X, respectively; covers are nontrivial, an ω-cover is one in which every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some member, a γ-cover is an infinite cover whose members contain each x ∈ X all but finitely often, S1(A,B) means that for every sequence (Un)n∈N of members of A one can choose Un ∈ Un so that {Un : n ∈ N} ∈ B, and Sfin(A,B) means that for every such sequence one can choose finite Fn ⊆ Un so that ⋃n Fn ∈ B. Does CH imply that, for each of the five exact satisfaction-patterns corresponding respectively to settings (d), (e), (g), (j), and (l) in Figure 4, there exists a set of reals X whose satisfied properties among the seven Borel-case nodes S1(BΓ,BΓ), S1(BΓ,BΩ), Sfin(B,B), Sfin(BΩ,BΩ), S1(BΩ,BΓ), S1(BΩ,BΩ), and S1(B,B) are exactly one of the following sets: {S1(BΓ,BΩ), Sfin(B,B)}; {S1(BΓ,BΩ), Sfin(B,B), S1(B,B)}; {S1(BΓ,BΩ), Sfin(B,B), Sfin(BΩ,BΩ), S1(B,B)}; {S1(BΓ,BΓ), S1(BΓ,BΩ), Sfin(B,B), S1(B,B)}; {S1(BΓ,BΓ), S1(BΓ,BΩ), Sfin(B,B), Sfin(BΩ,BΩ), S1(B,B)}? ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))
justification: Section 1 of the paper supplies the definitions of S1 and Sfin and of ω-covers and γ-covers. Section 3.3 then introduces the Borel classes B, BΩ, and BΓ and gives the complete Borel Scheepers diagram in Figure 2. Section 4 explains that one records, for a set of reals X, which nodes of that Borel diagram hold, lists all 14 consistent bullet/circle settings in Figure 4, notes which settings are already realized under CH (and which seem reachable by forcing arguments), and finally isolates the remaining CH question as Problem 4.1. So your draft is aimed very precisely at Problem 4.1, but to be fully stand-alone it must replace the bare Figure-4 labels by the exact property-patterns they encode. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))
